evidence.quote: Question 3.1. (1) Is Diff 0 (S3 , vol) uniformly perfect?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $S^3$ denote the standard 3-sphere equipped with its standard volume form $\mathrm{vol}$. Let $\mathrm{Diff}_0(S^3,\mathrm{vol})$ denote the identity component of the group of $C^\infty$ volume-preserving diffeomorphisms of $S^3$. A group $G$ is called uniformly perfect if there exists a positive integer $N$ such that every element of $G$ can be written as a product of at most $N$ commutators of elements of $G$ (in particular, $G$ must equal its own commutator subgroup).

Question: Is $\mathrm{Diff}_0(S^3,\mathrm{vol})$ uniformly perfect?
artifact.status_search_result: The question is posed as an open problem. Known results (Tsuboi, Burago–Ivanov–Polterovich) establish uniform perfectness of identity components of diffeomorphism groups in many settings, but the case of the volume-preserving diffeomorphism group of $S^3$ does not appear to be resolved in the available literature.

status_evidence.title: Uniform perfectness of diffeomorphism groups, I
status_evidence.snippet: Uniform perfectness results for diffeomorphism groups by Tsuboi and others, leaving certain volume-preserving cases open.
status_evidence.claim: Uniform perfectness of diffeomorphism groups is established in many cases but volume-preserving cases on low-dimensional manifolds remain delicate.

status_evidence.title: Volume-Preserving Diffeomorphism Groups (Banyaga)
status_evidence.snippet: Banyaga's structure theorems for groups of volume-preserving diffeomorphisms; perfectness is known but uniform perfectness is a finer property.
status_evidence.claim: Perfectness of the identity component of the volume-preserving diffeomorphism group is classical (Thurston-Banyaga), while uniform perfectness is a stronger open question in many cases.
